data.title: PDF to Text, a challenging problem
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 提取PDF中的文本信息比看起来更具挑战性，因为PDF本质上是图形格式，而非文本格式，其内容是通过将字形映射到“纸张”上的坐标来呈现的，可能存在旋转、重叠和乱序排列，语义信息很少。为了满足搜索引擎对干净HTML输入的需求，理想的方法是通过基于视觉的机器学习模型，但这在处理数百GB的PDF时难以扩展。现有的工具如PDFBox的PDFTextStripper可以提取文本，但无法识别标题等语义信息。为了改进，可以采用基于每页统计字体大小的方法来识别标题，通常比每页的中位数字体大小大20%的文本可能是标题。此外，处理多行标题和段落识别也是棘手的问题，需要进一步优化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PDF文本提取、OCR技术、PDF内容解析工具及其应用

不同观点：
• [90s_dev] 提到自己曾经精通某些PDF和OCR技术，但后来忘记了这些技能，直到重新接触相关项目才回忆起来。他具体提到使用过Tesseract OCR引擎，但对PDF内部结构的遗忘引发了对过去成就的反思。
• [svat] 希望有一个类似浏览器开发者工具的PDF查看工具，可以直观地查看PDF内容流和其生成的像素，类似于HTML页面的"查看源代码"功能。他认为现有的工具只停留在PDF对象层面，无法深入到内容流。
• [kbyatnal] 认为"PDF到文本"的转换可以分为不同类别的问题，包括OCR、结构化数据提取和端到端文档处理管道。他强调了OCR的商品化趋势，但指出从OCR输出到生产环境中的文档管道的构建仍然复杂，需要人工干预和精细调整。
• [dwheeler] 主张在PDF中嵌入可编辑的源文档，如LibreOffice所实现的那样，这样可以提供更好的信息和文本意义，同时与现有PDF阅读器兼容。
• [patrick41638265] 推荐使用pdftotext工具和Python脚本进行简单的PDF文本提取，适用于不太复杂的文档。
• [ted_dunning] 提供了一个具体的PDF例子，展示了多栏文本、页眉变化和段落格式不一致等复杂排版问题，强调了PDF解析的挑战。
• [1vuio0pswjnm7] 提供了一个简单的文本格式PDF示例，展示了如何通过文本编辑器直接修改PDF内容，强调了PDF的文本性质。

补充讨论：
• [bartread] 提到从PDF中提取表格数据非常困难，相比HTML文档的解析更加复杂，推荐使用Poppler PDF工具转换PDF为HTML再进行处理。
• [gibsonf1] 介绍了一种从PDF中创建"思想单元"并进行搜索和发现的方法，强调了语义层面的处理。
• [Sharlin] 赞扬了PDF阅读器中实现查找、选择和复制操作的开发者，认为这些功能的实现非常不易。
• [noosphr] 分享了从金融服务PDF中提取信息的经验，推荐使用分割模型和OCR模型，并指出VLM（视觉语言模型）在处理嵌套数据和长文本方面的不足。
• [elpalek] 测试了Gemini 2.5 Pro的OCR性能，发现直接提取PDF文本效果不佳，但转换为JPG后效果显著改善。
• [bob1029] 认为PDF到文本的解析在一般情况下类似于JPEG到文本的解析，唯一愿意署名的场景是从标准化文档中提取AcroForm字段值。
• [xnx] 指出文章中未提及LLMs（大型语言模型），认为LLMs在OCR和文档数据提取方面有显著改进。
• [wrs] 建议尝试使用传统的机器学习方法来解决PDF数据提取问题，而不是一味依赖LLMs。

争议焦点：
• 不同工具和方法在处理复杂PDF文档时的效果和可靠性。
• OCR和VLM在处理嵌套数据、长文本和表格数据提取方面的局限性。
• 使用LLMs与传统机器学习方法在PDF数据提取中的优劣比较。

43973721.article_content:
PDF to Text, a challenging problem
Posted: 2025-05-13
The search engine has recently gained the ability to index the PDF file format. The change will deploy over a few months.
Extracting text information from PDFs is a significantly bigger challenge than it might seem.
The crux of the problem is that the file format isn’t a text format at all, but a graphical format.
It doesn’t have text in the way you might think of it, but more of a mapping of glyphs to coordinates on “paper”. These
glyphs may be rotated, overlap, and appear out of order, with very little semantic information
attached to them.
You should probably be in awe at the fact that you can open a PDF file in your favorite viewer (or browser), hit ctrl+f, and search for text.
Vertical, rotated text, next to horizontal text.
Meanwhile the search engine preferrably wants clean HTML as input.
The absolute best way of doing this is these days is likely through a vision based machine learning model,
but that is an approach that is very far away from scaling to processing hundreds of gigabytes of PDF files
off a single server with no GPU.
Thankfully this isn’t a completely unexplored problem, it was possible to start off with
PDFBox
’
PDFTextStripper class, which
sort of
solves the problem, but with a lot of limitations that means
it isn’t quite suitable fo the search engine’s needs, as it does as it says on the box, extract the text from a PDF
with no regards for headings or other semantics, which are incredibly important relevance signals.
Following are some of the modifications made to provide a pdf-to-text extraction that is better suited to the search engine’s needs.
Identifying headings
A simple way we can look for headings is to seek a semibold or heavier line of text that is isolated from other
text, this works when headings are bolded, but not all headings are bolded!
Excerpt of the first page of "Can Education be Standardized? Evidence from Kenya", working version
As we see in the example above, many headings instead rely on font size instead.
This poses a problem, as font-sizes are very much specific to the document itself, one document may have its
body in 10pt with 16pt headings, another may use 14pt and 20pt instead! Finding a global breakpoint is futile,
instead it’s more effective to build some font size statistics instead.
Distribution of font sizes in "Can Education be Standardized?"
Here page 1 is the front page with an abstract and author listing, page 9 is text with a heading, and page 10 is just text.
There is some degree of noisiness to the font size distribution caused by subscripts, footnotes, and so forth.
We can see the distributions of pages 9 and 10 are fairly similar, but page 1 deviates significantly.
For each page there tends to be one dominant font size, which is generally the body text (note the logarithmic y-scale).
The differences in distribution hints that we may want to use not per-document statistics, but per-page statistics, since particularly the font choices on the first page often deviates from the rest. In the case of “Can education be standardized…”, font size 17 is used for the title of the document, but font size 14 is used for headings later on.
Attaching some factor of about 20% to the median font size of each page seems to fairly reliably identify headings. There are of course always exceptions,
but this catches most of the important cases.
Joining consecutive headings
Headings are often split into multiple lines, often for stylistic reasons. This means we sometimes want to join consecutive lines of heading text into one,
and deciding when to perform this operation is not entirely trivial. I won’t provide any real solution to this, but mostly try to highlight why it’s a tricky problem.
An example of a multiline heading, right justified, followed by additional bolded text.
The case above combines a two-line title with the popular aesthetic choice of a heading justified to the right–which casuses problems as indenting a line is also often an indicator of a paragraph break–following the title is another semibolded line of text (the author’s name) and some lines down we have a heading that is not bolded at all.
This is another case where we’re unlikely to find a fool-proof rule for joining. Joining consecutive headings with the same font size and weight seems to mostly do a good job, but there are plenty of cases where it produces undesirable results.
An example of two unrelated headings following each other with similar font size and weight.
Identifying Paragraphs
PDFTextStripper does a decent job of identifying paragraphs. It uses a clever mix of looking at line spacing and indentation to figure out when to break a paragraph. It does have some room for improvement though, particularly with regards to the line spacing logic.
Its biggest problem is that it uses a fixed break point for line separation where above that point, lines are not in the same paragraph, not taking account for the fact that documents us

data.title: Membrane: Media Framework for Elixir
data.author: lawik
data.article_summary: Membrane是一个易于理解和定制的多媒体框架，支持实时通信（WebRTC SFU）、服务器端处理（视频缩放、音频混合等）、多种可切换的输入/输出协议（WebRTC、HLS、RTP等），并能与任何Elixir应用无缝集成。它支持转码多种流行编解码器，提供监控工具，并被Firework、Keep In Mind等公司用于直播和视频处理。Membrane是免费开源的，由Software Mansion开发，并拥有活跃的社区支持，用户可以通过GitHub、Twitter、Discord等平台参与和获取帮助。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Elixir中的高性能媒体流框架的评价和讨论

不同观点：
• [积极评价] victorbjorklund认为该项目非常酷，即使没有用于严肃项目，单凭能够在Elixir中拥有高性能的媒体流框架就已经很了不起。他还提到可以用BEAM构建类似Twitch的应用，尽管建议搭配Postgres数据库。
• [开发体验] nw05678表示在使用Elixir的开发过程中，感觉开发环境不如其他语言流畅。
• [技术前景] Sean-Der称赞该项目的团队非常优秀，并提到开发者以正确的方式构建项目，而不仅仅是修修补补。他还特别提到对PeerConnection统计的可视化以及视频合成器的实时修改功能印象深刻。
• [实际应用] AlphaWeaver提到他们在工作中使用Erlang和Elixir，并且该项目是他们用于严肃项目的首选。但他提醒部分组件使用自定义许可证，尽管大部分是Apache 2.0开源许可证。

补充讨论：
• [教程需求] kingofheroes询问是否有人知道好的、最新的Elixir和Phoenix框架教程，表明他对重新学习该技术有兴趣。
• [技术选择] mml表达了对Nvidia没有选择类似技术而是选择gstreamer的失望，暗示对该项目的技术方向有不同看法。

争议焦点：
• 开发环境的流畅性：nw05678对Elixir的开发体验有保留意见，而其他评论者则多为积极评价，形成对比。
• 许可证问题：AlphaWeaver提醒大家注意该项目部分组件的自定义许可证，这可能会影响其在某些项目中的使用。

43945483.article_content:
your multimedia
solution
An easily understandable and customisable multimedia framework.
What can you do with Membrane?
Real Time Communication
WebRTC SFU implementation with modular architecture for custom I/O. Perfect for applying processing, dumping media at any stage, or creating additional non-WebRTC outputs.
Server-side processing
Video scaling, framerate conversion, cut & merge and text overlay. Audio mixing, resampling and fading. With easy option to create and add custom ones.
Multiple and switchable I/O protocols
Existing implementations of WebRTC, HLS, RTP, RTSP, RTMP, File, Http chunks, integration with speech to text utilities.
Seamless integration with any Elixir app
Membrane is built in Elixir. It reaps the benefits of Elixir's scalability and fault tolerance. But also because of that Mebrane's pipelines can easily become a part of any Elixir application, e.g. a web server built with Phoenix.
Transcoding
From and to many popular codecs: aac, opus, mpeg, h264, vp9, vp8.
Monitoring utilities
Tools to monitor pipeline health and EVM performance to ease debugging process.

data.article_summary: 本文讨论了调试技能的重要性及其常被忽视的现状，强调了通过重现错误、使用调试器逐行检查代码来识别和解决问题的方法。作者特别提到了一种常见错误——拼写错误（Typo），这种错误通常不会引发逻辑问题，但可能导致代码行为异常。拼写错误有时难以发现，因为大脑会自动“纠正”它们。为减少拼写错误，作者建议开启编译器警告、使用代码格式化工具，以及通过改进编码习惯（如使用更具区分性的变量名）来降低错误概率。尽管每个人容易犯的拼写错误不同，但通过持续的小改进，可以有效减少此类错误的发生。

主要讨论点：软件调试策略及相关工具、方法和责任归属

不同观点：
• [mannykannot] 提出在调试时，首先应花时间思考可能导致错误的因素。他认为在错误发生前思考可能出什么问题，比思考已经出现什么问题更加有效，因为后者是一个更加封闭的问题。

• [alilleybrinker] 提到可以利用Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) 这一长期存在的软件弱点分类法来帮助识别和分类错误。CWE提供了一个系统化的弱点分类资源，可以作为调试的参考。

• [marginalia_nu] 指出一种常见的设计缺陷子类别，即代码完全按照预期运行，但由于某些错误的假设，导致没有产生预期的效果。这个观点强调了在调试时需要检查代码背后的逻辑和假设。

43974026.article_content:
Debugging is often an undervalued skill. It’s not really taught in schools (as far as I know),
instead, you kind of have to pick it up as you go along. Today, I’ll try to remedy that by looking
at some common bugs and what to do about them.
The default strategy I use with any bug is to:
Try to find a way of reliably reproducing the bug so that I can
break into the debugger when the bug happens and
step through the code line by line to
see how what it
is
doing differs from what I
think
it should be doing.
Once you understand how the code’s
actual
behavior differs from your
mental model
of its
behavior, it is typically easy to identify the problem and fix it.
I know that there are some very successful programmers that don’t really use debuggers but instead
rely completely on
printf()
and logging. But I don’t really understand
how
they do it. Trying
to understand what the code is doing by inserting one
printf()
at a time and then re-running the
tests seems so much more inefficient than using a debugger. If you’ve never really used a debugger
(I know, they don’t teach these things in school), I suggest you try it! Get comfortable with
stepping through the code and examining what it does.
Of course, there are some situations where you
can’t
capture the bug in the debugger and have to
resort to other methods, but we’ll get to that later, so let’s get started.
The Typo
Unlike most other bugs, the
Typo
is not caused by any flawed reasoning. You had the right idea,
you just happened to type something else. Luckily, most typos are caught by the compiler, but
sometimes your boo-boos compile:
if
(set_x)
pos.x
=
new_pos.x;
if
(set_y)
pos.x
=
new_pos.y;
if
(set_y)
pos.z
=
new_pos.z;
Once you
see
them, typos are trivial to fix. The hard part is seeing them in the first place.
Typos can be hard to spot because just as when you read text with spelling errors, your brain
auto-corrects the code as you read it. To be good at proofreading, you have to force your brain to
go into a different mode where it focuses more on the
text itself
than the
meaning of the text
.
This can be tricky, but you get better with practice.
If you can’t spot the typo just from reading the code, you can switch to our default debugging
method — stepping through the code line by line and checking that each line does what you expect
it to.
How can you prevent typos? It might seem that there is nothing you can do. Your brain will just
glitch every once in a while and there is nothing you can do to stop it.
I don’t believe in such fatalism. Instead, I subscribe to the philosophy of
continuous small
improvements
. The goal is not to be perfect, the goal is to do a little better each day and over
time the accumulation of all those small improvements will add up to big gains.
So let’s try again.
How can you make typos a little less likely?
First, you should enable as many compiler warnings as possible and also tell the compiler to
treat warnings as errors. The goal is to have the compiler detect as many typos as possible so that
you can fix them before they turn into actual bugs.
A warning that makes a big difference for me is
-Wshadow
.
-Wshadow
makes it an error to reuse a
variable name in a sub-scope. This prevents stupid mistakes like:
int
test
=
x;
{
int
test
=
f();
g(test);
// <-- Meant to use `test` from outer scope.
}
Before I enabled
-Wshadow
, I made a lot of these mistakes. Mostly with very generic variable
names, such as
i
or
x
.
Second, use a source code formatter and run all your source code through it. We use
clang-format
and run it automatically on
Save
and
git commit
. The source code formatter can
sometimes reveal typos. For example, if you type this:
if
(x
>
max);
max
=
x;
the source code formatter will change it to:
if
(x
>
max)
;
max
=
x;
Which makes the bug more obvious.
Another thing you can do is to write things in a way that produces fewer typos. For example, I
used to write for-loops like this:
for
(uint32_t i
=
0
; i
<
tm_carray_size(items);
++
i) {
child_t
*
children
=
get_children(items[i]);
for
(uint32_t j
=
0
; j
<
tm_carray_size(children);
++
j)
...
}
However, I noticed that this would often result in typos where I would write
children[i]
instead
of
children[j]
. So I started changing to:
for
(uint32_t item_i
=
0
; item_i
<
tm_carray_size(items);
++
item_i) {
child_t
*
children
=
get_children(items[item_i]);
for
(uint32_t child_i
=
0
; child_i
<
tm_carray_size(children);
++
child_i)
...
}
With this, I’m much less likely to write
children[item_i]
. These days, I’ve switched to just
iterating over the pointers instead:
for
(
const
item_t
*
i
=
items,
*
ie
=
tm_carray_end(items); i
!=
ie;
++
i) {
child_t
*
children
=
get_children(
*
i);
for
(
const
child_t
*
c
=
children,
*
ce
=
tm_carray_end(children); c
!=
ce;
++
c)
...
}
Since
i
and
c
now have different types, it is impossible to confuse them. And if I would
accidentally write
*ce = tm_carray_end(items)
this would also give a compile error.
Everybody makes different typos, so

data.title: GOP sneaks decade-long AI regulation ban into spending bill
data.author: Jtsummers
data.article_summary: House Republicans introduced a budget provision to block state and local governments from regulating AI for 10 years, aiming to preempt both existing and future AI laws. This would impact laws like California's requirement for health care AI disclosure and New York's bias audits for AI hiring tools. The broad language could also affect federal funding allocations for state AI programs and limit debate on AI policy. The proposal has faced backlash from tech safety groups and Democrats, who argue it favors Big Tech and weakens consumer protections against AI risks. The move aligns with the Trump administration's industry-friendly AI policies, which include reversing Biden-era safety measures. Critics see this as a "gift to Big Tech" and a threat to state autonomy in AI governance.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国关于人工智能（AI）系统的监管与立法问题，特别是在自主车辆和自动化决策系统方面的监管缺位及其潜在影响。

不同观点：
• **支持监管的观点**：
   - [mikeweiss]：认为自主车辆（包括公交车和卡车）即将上路，现在是一个制定规则的好时机，例如让车辆礼让公共交通、优化交通流量等。这将有利于公众，而不仅仅是单个乘客。
   - [nimbius]：认为如果没有监管，将摧毁消费者对本已糟糕的市场的信心。AI系统需要有一定的问责机制。
   - [vonneumannstan]：认为阻止所有对AI的监管长达10年是疯狂的，不可接受。
   - [parliament32]：提到欧盟正在朝相反的方向发展，即通过《人工智能法》加强监管，暗示美国应效仿。

• **反对监管或支持有限/不同形式监管的观点**：
   - [tantalor]：认为目前没有法律定义的AI，因此通过法律限制AI系统是容易规避的。建议法律可以更广泛地涵盖计算机化系统，而非仅限于AI。
   - [bgwalter]：指出州和地方政府不能监管AI，但领导层仍可以通过行政命令干预，比如反对AI的“政治正确性”。还提到共和党一年前曾希望进行监管，但如今立场可能发生变化。

• **对监管可行性和法律效力的质疑**：
   - [cmeacham98]：质疑该法案的合法性，提出是否违反了美国宪法第十修正案。
   - [henning]：用讽刺的方式指出，如果要对所有“自动化决策系统”进行监管，那么像咖啡机中的PID控制器、人工耳蜗等是否也应该受到监管，暗示一刀切式的监管不切实际。

• **对潜在问题的担忧**：
   - [agentultra]：担心未来可能出现的问题，并质疑是否能在有能力的领导者上台后撤销不当政策。
   - [ndiddy]：批评在涉及大科技公司游说资金时，某些政客对“州权”的支持是选择性的，而非一贯的立场。
   - [DebtDeflation]：具体提到如果银行的自动化贷款审批系统存在种族歧视问题，该法案是否会阻止州政府采取行动，表现出对潜在不公正的忧虑。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于是否应对AI系统进行监管，特别是对自主车辆和自动化决策系统的规则制定。
• 一部分人支持立即制定规则以规范AI行为，而另一部分人则认为不应由州和地方政府监管，或认为监管本身可能不具备实际操作性。
• 欧盟与美国在AI监管上的对比也显示出跨地域监管差异的讨论。

On Sunday night, House Republicans added language to the Budget Reconciliation bill that would block all state and local governments from regulating AI for 10 years,
404 Media
reports. The provision, introduced by Representative Brett Guthrie of Kentucky,
states
that "no State or political subdivision thereof may enforce any law or regulation regulating artificial intelligence models, artificial intelligence systems, or automated decision systems during the 10 year period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act."
The broad wording of the proposal would prevent states from enforcing both existing and proposed laws designed to protect citizens from AI systems. For example, California's
recent law
requiring health care providers to disclose when they use generative AI to communicate with patients would potentially become unenforceable. New York's 2021 law
mandating bias audits
for AI tools used in hiring decisions would also be affected, 404 Media notes. The measure would also halt legislation set to take effect in 2026 in California that requires AI developers to
publicly document
the data used to train their models.
The ban could also restrict how states allocate federal funding for AI programs. States currently control how they use federal dollars and can direct funding toward AI initiatives that may conflict with the administration's technology priorities. The Education Department's
AI programs
represent one example where states might pursue different approaches than those favored by the White House and its tech industry allies.
The House Committee on Energy and Commerce, chaired by Guthrie,
scheduled consideration
of the text during the budget reconciliation markup on May 13. The language defines AI systems broadly enough to encompass both newer generative AI tools and older automated decision-making technologies.
The reconciliation bill primarily focuses on cuts to Medicaid access and increased health care fees for millions of Americans. The AI provision appears as an addition to these broader health care changes, potentially limiting debate on the technology's policy implications.
The move is already inspiring backlash. On Monday, tech safety groups and at least one Democrat criticized the proposal, reports
The Hill
. Rep. Jan Schakowsky (D-Ill.), the ranking member on the Commerce, Manufacturing and Trade Subcommittee, called the proposal a "giant gift to Big Tech," while nonprofit groups like the Tech Oversight Project and Consumer Reports warned it would leave consumers unprotected from AI harms like deepfakes and bias.
Big Tech’s White House connections
President Trump has already
reversed
several Biden-era executive orders on AI safety and risk mitigation. The push to prevent state-level AI regulation represents an escalation in the administration's industry-friendly approach to AI policy.
Perhaps it's no surprise, as the AI industry has cultivated close ties with the Trump administration since before the president took office. For example, Tesla CEO Elon Musk
serves
in the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), while entrepreneur David Sacks acts as
"AI czar,"
and venture capitalist Marc Andreessen reportedly
advises
the administration. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman
appeared with Trump
in an AI datacenter development plan announcement in January.
By limiting states' authority over AI regulation, the provision could prevent state governments from using federal funds to develop AI oversight programs or support initiatives that diverge from the administration's
deregulatory stance
. This restriction would extend beyond enforcement to potentially affect how states design and fund their own AI governance frameworks.

   - [parliament32]：提到欧盟正在朝相反的方向发展，即通过《人工智能法》加强监管，暗示美国应效仿。

• **反对监管或支持有限/不同形式监管的观点**：
   - [tantalor]：认为目前没有法律定义的AI，因此通过法律限制AI系统是容易规避的。建议法律可以更广泛地涵盖计算机化系统，而非仅限于AI。
   - [bgwalter]：指出州和地方政府不能监管AI，但领导层仍可以通过行政命令干预，比如反对AI的“政治正确性”。还提到共和党一年前曾希望进行监管，但如今立场可能发生变化。

• **对监管可行性和法律效力的质疑**：
   - [cmeacham98]：质疑该法案的合法性，提出是否违反了美国宪法第十修正案。
   - [henning]：用讽刺的方式指出，如果要对所有“自动化决策系统”进行监管，那么像咖啡机中的PID控制器、人工耳蜗等是否也应该受到监管，暗示一刀切式的监管不切实际。

• **对潜在问题的担忧**：
   - [agentultra]：担心未来可能出现的问题，并质疑是否能在有能力的领导者上台后撤销不当政策。
   - [ndiddy]：批评在涉及大科技公司游说资金时，某些政客对“州权”的支持是选择性的，而非一贯的立场。
   - [DebtDeflation]：具体提到如果银行的自动化贷款审批系统存在种族歧视问题，该法案是否会阻止州政府采取行动，表现出对潜在不公正的忧虑。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于是否应对AI系统进行监管，特别是对自主车辆和自动化决策系统的规则制定。
• 一部分人支持立即制定规则以规范AI行为，而另一部分人则认为不应由州和地方政府监管，或认为监管本身可能不具备实际操作性。
• 欧盟与美国在AI监管上的对比也显示出跨地域监管差异的讨论。

data.title: PyPI Organizations (2023)
data.author: calpaterson
data.article_summary: PyPI推出组织账户功能，作为其增强平台财务支持和长期可持续性计划的第一步。组织账户允许团队拥有专属的品牌网址，便于管理多个子团队和软件包，特别适合大型社区项目或公司。社区项目可免费使用，企业项目则需支付少量费用，收入将用于提升PyPI的支持和基础设施。PyPI去年下载量达2357亿次，年增长57%，新收入将帮助平台更好地应对支持需求。组织功能是可选的，现有用户不受影响。社区和企业项目现可申请组织名称，审批将在数周内进行，企业项目的付费细节将在5月确定。这项开发得到了Python软件基金会和赞助商的支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[PyPI服务的运营及其功能改进建议]

不同观点：
• [alexchantavy] 认为PyPI是一个重要的服务，用户通常会认为其运行良好而不加注意。他分享了自己在进行GitHub仓库到PyPI的配置更新时，经历了密码丢失和账户恢复的过程，意识到PyPI处理了大量其他组织的工作，且运营工作繁重。他提到了账户恢复的相关问题链接。

• [joshdavham] 指出，截至2023年，创建组织仍然需要申请审批，且审批过程缓慢。他提到自己的朋友在去年秋天申请了一个组织，但至今尚未获得批准。

• [hobofan] 仅标注了年份[2023]，未提供额外观点，但支持了对该年份的讨论背景。

43975541.article_content:
Introducing PyPI Organizations
Today, we are rolling out the first step in our plan to build financial
support and long-term sustainability of the Python Packaging Index (PyPI),
while simultaneously giving our users one of our most requested features:
organization accounts.
Introducing Organizations
Organizations on PyPI are self-managed teams, with their own exclusive branded
web addresses. Our goal is to make PyPI easier to use for large community
projects, organizations, or companies who manage multiple sub-teams and multiple
packages. We’re making organizations available to community projects for free,
forever, and to corporate projects for a small fee. Additional priority support
agreements will be available to all paid subscribers, and all revenue will go
right back into PyPI to continue building better support and infrastructure
for all our users.
Increasing sustainability and support
In the last year PyPI served 235.7 billion downloads for the 448,941 projects hosted
there. This means that since the previous period, PyPI saw a 57% annual growth in download counts
and bandwidth alike. Having more people using and contributing to Python every
year is an fantastic problem to have, but it is one we must increase
organizational capacity to accommodate.
Increased revenue for PyPI allows it to become a
staffed platform that can respond to support requests and attend to issues
in a timeframe that is significantly faster than what our excellent (but thinly
spread) largely volunteer team could reasonably handle.
Organizations are opt-in
We want to be very clear—these new features are completely optional. If
features for larger projects don't sound like something that would be useful to
you as a PyPI maintainer, then there is no obligation to create an organization
and absolutely nothing about your PyPI experience will change for you.
A basis for future features
We look forward to discussing what other features PyPI users would like to see
tackled next. We know there are lots of ideas out there around safety,
security and usability and we’re looking forward to hearing about anything that
you think would benefit the community. And in the spirit of open source,
we
welcome your feedback
on what's on
offer so far.
Get started today
Both community projects (non-profits, NGO’s, hobbyists, etc) and corporate
teams can
sign up to request their organization name starting
today
. Submissions will begin
seeing review and approval in the coming weeks, and corporate teams will be
able to finalize their signup with billing details in May.
Acknowledgements
Organization feature development was approved by the
Packaging Working Group
and funded through the
Python Software Foundation
's
sponsorship program -- thanks to our
sponsors
for making this work possible.
We especially want to thank
Bloomberg
for funding our Packaging Project Manager, Shamika Mohanan.
We are also grateful for the many generous PyPI users who shared their
perspectives with Shamika, which laid the foundation for these new features.
And thanks as well to our beta
testers, including the following ✨new✨ PyPI organizations:
Python Cryptographic Authority (
https://pypi.org/org/pyca/
)
The Pallets Project (
https://pypi.org/org/pallets/
)
certifi (
https://pypi.org/org/certifi
)
Ee Durbin is the Director of Infrastructure at
the Python Software Foundation.
They have been contributing to keeping PyPI online, available, and
secure since 2013.
Back to top

data.title: Google is building its own DeX: First look at Android's Desktop Mode
data.author: logic_node
data.article_summary: Google正在开发一个名为"Desktop View"的桌面界面，旨在为Android手机提供类似PC的多任务体验。该功能包括一个持久的任务栏和可自由调整大小的窗口，类似于Windows或ChromeOS的界面。虽然仍在开发中，但"Desktop View"显示了Google在多任务处理能力上的进展。目前，三星DeX是将手机变成桌面体验的主要选项，而Google的新功能将提供一个更强大的桌面环境。该模式目前处于测试阶段，可能不会在Android 16中作为最终产品出现，但其开发表明Google正努力为用户提供替代DeX的选择，使手机能够成为真正的口袋电脑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：移动设备的桌面模式和虚拟显示功能的可行性、应用场景及未来发展

不同观点：
• **虚拟显示和任务栏问题**：[smusamashah] 提到 Scrcpy 支持虚拟显示，但默认的安卓系统在大分辨率下没有任务栏。虽然可以通过提高DPI来显示任务栏，但希望能进一步优化，让虚拟显示中也支持任务栏功能。
• **桌面模式与Linux终端集成的重要性**：[enragedcacti] 认为桌面模式的真正亮点在于与Google的Linux终端应用的集成，这样可以建立更舒适的开发环境，特别是对于Samsung DeX用户来说，能够运行完整的Linux应用将会是重大突破。
• **AR/XR与DeX结合的未来潜力**：[NBJack] 分享了自己使用Samsung DeX与AR眼镜结合的体验，认为这种组合在未来具有巨大的潜力，尤其是在工作场景中的应用，并期待Google与三星合作的"第一方"解决方案。
• **手机计算资源的充分利用**：[lanthissa] 和 [carlhjerpe] 都认为手机的计算能力已经足够强大，未来个人计算设备可能只需要一个手机和外围设备即可，不必再拥有多个独立的计算设备。他们还讨论了Linux容器的用户体验和手机散热问题。
• **桌面模式无需外部显示**：[simpaticoder] 希望桌面模式不需要依赖外部显示器，因为即使只用手机自带的显示屏，也可以完成很多编程任务，特别是对于一些轻量级的工作来说。
• **折叠手机与UI限制**：[the_clarence] 提到折叠手机提供了更大的屏幕空间，但当前的UI仍然感觉受限，期望未来能有更适合大屏幕的UI设计。
• **无线连接的需求**：[0xbadcafebee] 对桌面模式没有无线选项表示失望，认为这是功能的缺失，尤其是连Android Auto都有无线模式。
• **对桌面模式普及过晚的遗憾**：[nashashmi] 认为USB-C手机连接桌面dock实现全功能电脑的想法已经提出多年，但至今仍未实现，很多改进似乎来得太晚。
• **多任务处理的实用性**：[voidUpdate] 认为在普通手机上进行多任务处理不太实际，感觉会很局促，但在折叠手机上可能会更合适。
• **历史对比与反思**：[jasonlotito] 提到Windows Phone早在十多年前就实现了类似的功能，认为这是被遗忘的创新。[kome] 则对智能手机持批判态度，认为它们主要是消费工具，而非创造工具，期望一种更自由、更具创造力的个人计算设备。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到Samsung DeX和折叠手机的实际应用体验，尤其是它们在工作场景中的潜力。
• 有对未来计算设备形态的展望，包括手机作为主要计算设备，配合外围设备如键盘、显示器、AR眼镜等的使用场景。
• 争议焦点之一是桌面模式是否需要外部显示器，以及当前UI对大屏幕和多任务处理的支持程度。
• 另一个争议点是功能的实现速度和实用性，例如无线连接和Linux终端集成等功能的缺失。

Google is developing a new desktop interface called "Desktop View" for Android phones.
"Desktop View" will include features like a persistent taskbar and freeform, resizable windows.
While still a work in progress, the new desktop mode shows Google's progress towards offering a PC-like multitasking experience.
For years, if you’ve wanted to plug your Android phone into a monitor and get something that felt remotely like a desktop, your only option has essentially been Samsung DeX. It offers a proper multi-window interface, a taskbar, and the ability to use your phone like a PC. Meanwhile, Android’s offering for other devices has been extremely lacking. That appears to be changing.
Last year, Google finally allowed Pixel phones to
mirror their displays to external screens
. Then, earlier this year, Google was working on a
developer option for desktop mode
. Now, deep dives into the Android code are revealing Google's ambitions for a more robust desktop environment, currently dubbed "Desktop View." This isn't just a tweaked interface for tablets; it's designed to work when you connect your phone to an external display, giving you a layout that's far more conducive to getting work done with a keyboard and mouse.
“Desktop View” includes features such as a persistent taskbar, much like you'd find on Windows or ChromeOS. This bar will reportedly give you quick access to your pinned apps and show your recently used ones, making switching between tasks much smoother than the standard Android recent apps view. More importantly, the system is being built to handle multiple apps running in resizable, freeform windows. You can apparently also drag and drop content between windows if the apps support it. This is crucial for getting that true PC-like multitasking experience.
While this early desktop mode is showing significant progress, it's important to temper expectations slightly. First, it's still clearly a work in progress, tucked away in developer options in current beta builds. Right now, it's essentially a modified version of Android's windowing mode that you can currently see on tablets and foldables. So, it’s unlikely that we’ll see this as a finished product in
Android 16
.
Advertisement
Advertisement
However, the fact that Google is actively developing these features and building upon the basic windowing capabilities introduced in earlier Android versions is a good sign. Google has also been working on bringing
external display tools to Android
–things like the ability to rearrange displays and move a mouse between displays. It feels like Google is finally ready to offer an alternative to DeX for those who don’t want a Samsung phone, turning your phone into a real pocket computer.

主要讨论点：AI保险的性质、应用场景及其潜在问题

• **创新建议**（JumpCrisscross）：提出基础模型开发者可以承担首当其冲的损失，从而降低保费并增加模型使用率，这是一种创新的商业模式建议。

• **实际体验**（Neywiny）：分享了一次与AI打交道的负面经历，强调人类监督的重要性，并暗示当前AI技术尚不完善。

• **数据证据问题**（85392_school）：质疑AI保险的实际应用，因为目前没有证据表明大型语言模型会随着时间推移而退化，从而引发保险覆盖的情况。

• **类比人类保险**（yieldcrv）：建议AI应该像人类承包商一样购买错误和遗漏保险，这表明AI在某些工作中的角色与人类相似。

data.title: Mill as a direct style build tool
data.author: lihaoyi
data.article_summary: Mill是一个JVM构建工具，支持Java、Scala、Kotlin等多种语言，特别适合大规模单体代码库的构建，具有与Bazel类似的功能。Mill采用独特的“直接风格”设计，使其易于使用和扩展，并具有比Maven、Gradle等工具快3-6倍的构建速度。与传统构建工具不同，Mill允许用户编写“直接风格”代码定义构建逻辑，类似于React.js在UI开发中的创新。它支持增量编译、懒加载、自动缓存和并行化，能高效处理包含数百甚至数千模块的大型项目。Mill最初是Scala的构建工具，现已扩展至Java等其他平台，并在Scala社区中获得5-10%的市场份额。其设计简化了构建逻辑的编写和维护，提升了开发效率。

• [openplatypus] 提到Li Haoyi在一次演讲中展示了Java编译器的速度，并指出Maven和Gradle带来的开销问题。他认为尽管Mill是一个快速发展的优秀工具，但在IDE中的BSP支持仍在改进中，因此在JVM语言中，Maven和Gradle仍有优势。

• [vamega] 关注Mill是否计划实现类似Bazel的远程执行功能，显示出对构建工具功能扩展的兴趣。

• [fithisux] 认为构建工程工具通常被低估或隐藏在企业内部，强调了其在软件工程中的重要性。

Edit this Page Mill as a Direct Style Build Tool Mill is a JVM build tool that targets Java/Scala/Kotlin and has potential to serve the large-monorepo codebases that Bazel currently serves. Mill has good traction among its users, benchmarks that demonstrate 3-6x faster builds than its competitors, and a unique "direct-style" design that make it easy to use and extend. This page discusses some of the most interesting design decisions in Mill, and how it sets Mill apart from other build tools on the market. What is a Build Tool? A build tool is a program that coordinates the various tasks necessary to compile, package, test, and run a codebase: maybe you need to run a compiler, download some dependencies, package an executable or container. While a small codebase can get by with a shell script that runs every task every time one at a time, such a naive approach gets slower and slower as a codebase grows and the build tasks necessarily get more numerous and complex. In order to prevent development from grinding to a halt, you need to begin skipping the build tasks you do not need at any point in time, and caching and parallelizing those that you do. This often starts off as some ad-hoc if-else statements in a shell script, but manually maintaining skipping/caching/parallelization logic is tedious and error-prone. At some point it becomes worthwhile to use an purpose built tool to do it for you, and that is when you turn to build tools like Maven , Make , Mill , or Bazel . For this article, we will mostly discuss Mill. What is Mill? The Mill build tool was started in 2017, an exploration of the ideas I found when learning to use Google’s Bazel build tool. At a glance, Mill looks similar to other build tools you may be familiar with, with a build.mill file in the root of a project defining the dependencies and testing setup for a module: package build import mill._, javalib._ object foo extends JavaModule { def mvnDeps = Seq( mvn"net.sourceforge.argparse4j:argparse4j:0.9.0", mvn"org.thymeleaf:thymeleaf:3.1.1.RELEASE" ) object test extends JavaTests with TestModule.Junit4 } The syntax may be a bit unfamiliar, but anyone familiar with programming can probably guess what this build means: a JavaModule with two ivy dependencies argparse4j and thymeleaf , and a test submodule supporting Junit4 . This build can then be compiled, tested, run, or packaged into an assembly from the command line: > /mill foo.compile compiling 1 Java source... > /mill foo.run --text hello

hello

> ./mill foo.test Test foo.FooTest.testEscaping finished, ... Test foo.FooTest.testSimple finished, ... 0 failed, 0 ignored, 2 total, ... > ./mill show foo.assembly ".../out/foo/assembly.dest/out.jar" > ./out/foo/assembly.dest/out.jar --text hello

hello

Mill was originally a Scala build tool competing with sbt , and by 2023 it had reached around 5-10% market share in the Scala community ( Jetbrains Survey , VirtusLabs Survey ). It recently grew first-class Java support, demonstrating 3-6x speedups over existing Java build tools like Maven or Gradle. Mill also has gained experimental support for Java-adjacent platforms like Kotlin and Android , and has demonstrated the ability to branch out into supporting more distant toolchains like Typescript and Python . Mill also works well with large builds : its build logic can be split into multiple folders , is incrementally compiled, lazily initialized, and automatically cached and parallelized. That means that even large codebases can remain fast and responsive: Mill’s own build easily manages over 400 modules, and the tool can likely handle thousands of modules without issue. The React.js of Build Tools We’ve briefly covered what Mill is above, but one question remains: why Mill? Why not one of the other 100 build tools out there? Mill is unique in that it shares many of its core design decisions with React.js , the popular Javascript UI framework. I was among the first external users of React when I introduced it to Dropbox in 2014, and while people gripe about it today, React was really a revolution in how Javascript UIs were implemented. UI flows that used to take weeks suddenly took days, requiring a fraction of the code and complexity that they previously took to implement React’s two most important innovations are: Letting users write "direct style" code to define their UI - Javascript functions that directly returned the HTML structure you wanted - rather than a "code behind" approach of registering callbacks to mutate the UI in response to events Using a single "general purpose" programming language for your UI, rather than splitting your logic into multiple special-purpose domain-specific languages While React does a huge number of clever things - virtual dom diffing , JSX , de/re-hydration , etc. - all of those are only in service of the two fundamental ideas. e.g. At Dropbox we used React for years without JSX, and many of the later frameworks inspired by React provide a simil

data.title: Chrome's New Embedding Model: Smaller, Faster, Same Quality
data.author: kaycebasques
data.article_summary: Chrome的最新更新引入了一个新的文本嵌入模型，该模型比之前的版本缩小了57%（从81.91MB减少到35.14MB），同时在语义搜索任务中保持几乎相同的性能。模型缩小主要通过将嵌入矩阵从float32量化为int8精度实现，且未明显影响嵌入质量或搜索排名。新模型在架构上与旧模型相似，主要区别在于关键嵌入矩阵的量化，使得新模型的存储需求大幅下降。尽管内部进行了量化，新模型的输出嵌入仍保持完整的float32精度，甚至略有提高。用户将受益于更小的存储占用、更快的浏览器更新以及更高效的资源利用，而搜索质量保持不变。这一优化特别有利于存储空间有限的设备。

43973502.article_content:
Chrome’s New Embedding Model: Smaller, Faster, Same Quality
Apr 19, 2025
—
by
Dan Petrovic
in
Google
,
Machine Learning
TL;DR
Chrome’s latest update incorporates a new text embedding model that is 57% smaller (35.14MB vs 81.91MB) than its predecessor while maintaining virtually identical performance in semantic search tasks.
The size reduction was achieved primarily through quantization of the embedding matrix from float32 to int8 precision, with no measurable degradation in embedding quality or search ranking.
Discovery and Extraction
During routine analysis of Chrome’s binary components, I discovered a new version of the embedding model in the browser’s optimization guide directory. This model is used for history clustering and semantic search.
Model directory:
~/AppData/Local/Google/Chrome SxS/User Data/optimization_guide_model_store/57/A3BFD4A403A877EC/
Technical Analysis Methodology
To analyze the models, I developed a multi-faceted testing approach:
Model Structure Analysis
: Used TensorFlow’s interpreter to extract model architecture, tensor counts, shapes, and data types.
Binary Comparison
: Analyzed compression ratios, binary patterns, and weight distributions.
Weight Quantization Assessment
: Examined specific tensors to determine quantization techniques.
Output Precision Testing
: Estimated effective precision of output embeddings by analyzing minimum differences between adjacent values.
Semantic Search Evaluation
: Compared similarity scores and result rankings across multiple queries using a test corpus.
Key Findings
1. Architecture Comparison
Both models maintain identical architecture with similar tensor counts (611 vs. 606) and identical input/output shapes ([1,64] input and [1,768] output). This suggests they were derived from the same base model, likely a transformer-based embedding architecture similar to BERT.
2. Quantization Details
The primary difference is in the embedding matrix, which stores token representations:
Old model:
arith.constant30: [32128, 512], <class 'numpy.float32'>, 62.75 MB
New model:
tfl.pseudo_qconst57: [32128, 512], <class 'numpy.int8'>, 15.69 MB
This single tensor accounts for approximately 47MB of the total 46.77MB size reduction. The model contains 58 pseudo-quantized tensors in both versions, but the critical embedding matrix was converted from float32 to int8.
3. Output Precision Analysis
Despite internal quantization, the new model’s output embeddings maintain full float32 precision:
Old model: Estimated bits of precision = 22.59 bits
New model: Estimated bits of precision = 25.42 bits
Intriguingly, the new model shows slightly higher effective precision, suggesting sophisticated quantization-aware training techniques.
4. Semantic Search Performance
Testing on diverse queries (e.g. “climate solutions”, “machine learning applications”, “travel documents”) showed:
Virtually identical similarity scores (differences of 0.001-0.004)
Identical result rankings for most queries
Slight speed improvement (1-2% faster inference)
Binary Structure Analysis
Detailed comparison of the binary files revealed:
60% reduction in int8 zero bytes but 48.5% increase in float32 zero bytes
53.3% increase in runs of zeros, indicating different storage strategies
Float tensor size reduction from 67.33MB to 5.05MB
Both models have similar compression ratios when further compressed (1.10x vs. 1.11x)
Implications
This optimization represents a significant achievement in model compression for edge devices. By selectively quantizing the largest tensor while preserving the architecture and output precision, Chrome’s engineers have achieved a substantial size reduction without compromising semantic search quality.
The approach demonstrates how selective quantization of specific model components can be more effective than blanket quantization strategies. This technique is particularly valuable for browsers and other edge applications where storage efficiency is critical but performance cannot be sacrificed.
The slightly higher effective precision in the output layer suggests the quantization process may have included fine-tuning to compensate for potential precision loss, resulting in a model that maintains or even slightly improves embedding quality.
User Impact and Benefits
This optimization delivers several tangible benefits for Chrome users:
Reduced Storage Footprint
: The 46.77MB size reduction frees up valuable storage space, particularly important on devices with limited capacity like budget smartphones and tablets.
Faster Browser Updates
: Smaller ML models result in smaller browser updates, reducing download times and data usage during Chrome’s update process.
Improved Resource Efficiency
: The slightly faster inference time (1-2%) contributes to more responsive browser performance when using features that rely on the embedding model, such as history search and content clustering.
Consistent Quality
: Users receive these storage and performance benefits with no degradation in search

data.article_summary: theForger's Win32 API Programming Tutorial是一份指导开发者使用Win32 API进行编程的教程。它涵盖了基础知识，如创建简单窗口、处理消息、资源使用、菜单和图标、对话框、标准控件、多文档界面、图形设备接口、位图和设备环境、计时器与动画、文本、字体和颜色等。教程建议按顺序阅读，每节内容相互关联，并提供了常见错误解决方案。完整示例代码需单独下载。教程有多种语言翻译版本，但这些版本可能未包含最新更新和修复。版权归Brook Miles所有。

主要讨论点：Windows 编程中手动管理资源（如句柄）的挑战及其学习过程

不同观点：
• [dnamlin] 认为在 OLE/COM 之前，需要记住按正确顺序释放许多句柄，这是相当复杂的。他提到使用 C++ 包装器和 RAII（资源获取即初始化）机制来管理资源，这在 "smart pointers"（智能指针）出现之前需要多次迭代和理解。他还表达了对 #winprog IRC 频道讨论的怀念，这些讨论以及一些教程和书籍帮助他学习并开始了像 Startup Control Panel 这样的项目。

• [gitroom] 表示对 [dnamlin] 的经历有共鸣，他也记得当时为了句柄泄漏问题而苦苦挣扎，认为处理这些问题是一种“入门仪式”。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了具体的资源管理技术，如 RAII 和 C++ 包装器，这些都是早期在没有智能指针的情况下管理资源的常见方法。
• 提到了影响深远的资源，如 theForger's 教程和 Charles Petzold 的书籍，这些都是 Windows 编程初学者的重要学习材料。
• 两人都对早期 Windows 编程的挑战持有一定的怀旧情感，认为这些经历是成长为熟练开发者的重要部分。
• 争议焦点并不明显，更多是一种对过去编程挑战的共同回忆和理解。

data.title: Detecting if an expression is constant in C
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了如何在C语言中创建一个宏，验证表达式是否为编译时常量，并在保持原始类型的情况下返回该常量。不同方法适用于不同的C标准和编译器支持情况：

1. **C23的constexpr复合字面量**：使用C23标准引入的`constexpr`和`typeof`，定义宏`#define C(x) ( (constexpr typeof(x)){x} )`，确保表达式为常量。缺点是C23尚未广泛支持。

2. **GNU扩展的`__builtin_constant_p`**：利用GNU扩展，通过`__builtin_choose_expr`选择常量表达式，否则触发编译错误。缺点是依赖GNU扩展。

3. **C11的`static_assert`**：使用C11的`static_assert`结合`sizeof`和匿名结构，验证表达式是否为常量。缺点是可能改变表达式类型。

4. **sizeof + 复合字面量和数组类型**：利用C99的变长数组特性，通过复合字面量验证常量。优点是无需C11支持，但继承了`static_assert`的问题。

5. **sizeof + 枚举常量**：利用枚举常量必须是整型常量表达式的特性，但存在枚举常量“泄漏”的问题。

不同方法各有优缺点，选择取决于具体需求和环境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何在编译期判断表达式是否为常量表达式，以及在C语言中处理此类问题的复杂性与可能的解决方案。

不同观点：
• [sleirsgoevy] 认为可以通过使用Linux内核中的一种技巧来判断表达式是否为编译时常量，而无需中断编译过程。他提供了一个宏定义 `__is_constexpr(x)`，并解释了其工作原理：利用三元表达式的特性，在常量表达式情况下返回特定类型的大小，从而进行判断。此外，他还提到可以通过一些技巧实现编译时的"类型三元表达式"（TYPE_IF），但未提供具体实现。

• [bobbyi] 尝试使用 `sizeof` 操作符来判断表达式是否为编译时常量，但遇到问题。他引用了标准中的规定，指出对于可变长度数组，`sizeof` 操作会在运行时计算，而不是编译时。这导致他的方法未能如预期工作。

• [wahern] 回应了关于编译器警告的问题，指出在使用匿名枚举时，GCC和Clang会发出警告。他提供了一种使用 `_Pragma` 来抑制警告的解决方案，但同时也提到GCC对 `_Pragma` 的使用位置更为严格，并且GCC 14没有合适的开关来禁用匿名枚举警告。

• [pjc50] 对上述复杂的技巧持批评态度，认为学习一种可以通过类型系统强制执行此类检查的语言会更好。他建议使用支持 `constexpr` 的语言版本，而不是依赖C语言中的这些技巧。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的具体实现技巧，如 `__is_constexpr(x)` 和 `C(x)`，展示了在C语言中处理编译时常量判断的复杂性。
• 编译器行为和警告处理也是讨论的一个重要方面，特别是如何抑制特定警告以及不同编译器之间的差异。
• 对使用现代C++特性（如 `constexpr`）的建议，反映了对更简洁和类型安全解决方案的需求。

Detecting if an expression is constant in C
21 Apr 2025
Here's a fun little language puzzle: implement a macro that takes an (integer or
floating) expression as an argument and:
Verifies that the expression is a constant expression (i.e, known at compile
time), otherwise aborts the compilation.
"Returns" back the same value.
Optionally, the returned value has the same type as the original expression.
There's a number of ways to solve this, depending on which C standard you're
using and whether compiler extensions are allowed or not.
Here are a few I've come across along with some pros and cons.
constexpr compound literals
If you're using C23 or later then you can specify a storage duration for
compound literals.
Combined with
typeof
and
constexpr
, both of which were also
standardized in C23, you can use the following:
#define C(x) ( (constexpr typeof(x)){x} )
This keeps the type intact, and since initializers of
constexpr
storage
duration need to be constant expression, the compiler will ensure that
x
is a
constant expression.
Cons:
Requires C23, which isn't widely supported as of this writing.
Clang (v20) doesn't seem to support storage durations in compound literals
just yet (GCC v14.2 seems to work).
Earlier version of this article used
static
instead of
constexpr
.
Since
static
storage duration requires initializer to be constant expression,
the compiler would ensure it.
However,
constexpr
has slightly better semantics here because unlike
static
,
constexpr
mandates that the
resulting
expression (not merely the
initializer) will also be a constant expression.
__builtin_constant_p
If using GNU extensions is not a problem, then you can use
__builtin_constant_p
, which returns true when an expression is constant
along with
__builtin_choose_expr
for selection.
__attribute((error("not constant"))) int notconst(void);
#define C(x) __builtin_choose_expr(__builtin_constant_p(x), (x), notconst())
When
__builtin_constant_p
returns true,
__builtin_choose_expr
picks the
first expression.
Otherwise, it calls a dummy non-existent function declared with the
error
attribute
, causing a compilation error.
Unlike ternary operator,
__builtin_choose_expr
isn't subject to the type
promotion rules and thus keeps the type of the expression intact.
Cons:
Requires GNU extensions.
static_assert
This trick was shown to me by constxd in an IRC channel and uses C11+
static_assert
to ensure the expression is static.
But how do we "return" the expression back? Well... with a bit of
sizeof
+
anon
struct
magic:
#define C(x) ((x) + 0*sizeof( \
struct { _Static_assert((int)(x) || 1, ""); char tmp; } \
))
This looks very wonky.
How is a
static_assert
allowed inside a struct declaration?
It's because the standard classifies
static_assert
as a declaration which
declares nothing (don't ask me why).
So syntactically, you can just put it inside a struct.
The addition by
0*sizeof(...)
is effectively a no-op, leaving the value
unchanged, but the type may change due to promotion.
Cons:
May change the type of the expression due to the addition, which is subject to
the typical integer promotion rules. (Though see the
comma
operator
section for a solution).
Standard says
the expression of
static_assert
needs to be an
integer constant expression, though gcc and clang seems to accept floating
point expression as well, but emits warnings.
(Note: the immediate
int
cast makes
floating constant
e.g
1.1
work, but
not things like
1.1 + 2.2
, without emitting warnings that is).
sizeof + compound literal with array type
This uses a similar trick as the above but instead of
static_assert
, it uses a
compound literal array type to ensure that the expression is constant:
#define C(x) ( (x) + 0*sizeof( (char [(int)(x) || 1]){0} ) )
A couple things to note:
Since C99, arrays (and array types) can be of variable length.
But compound literals do not accept variable-length types, which does the
verification for us.
Standard C (unfortunately) forbids zero-length arrays, hence the
|| 1
.
Array sizes beyond a certain limit cannot be declared (even if no storage is
being allocated).
On my 64 bit PC, gcc refuses sizes above
PTRDIFF_MAX
(2
63
-1)
bytes, and clang is even more conservative and rejects sizes above 61 bits.
Aside from supporting
0
, the
|| 1
also clamps down the array size to 1.
The only advantage of this approach over
static_assert
is that it doesn't
require C11 and can be used in C99.
Other than that it inherits all the problems that comes with
static_assert
:
The type may change.
Doesn't support floating expression (and unlike
static_assert
gcc refuses to
compile floating expression completely).
sizeof + enum constant
Because enum constants are required to be integer constant expression, we can
use them instead of compound literal:
#define C(x) ( (x) + 0*sizeof( enum { tmp = (int)(x) } ) )
However, there's one glaring issue with this: unlike the compound literal, the
enum constant "leaks out".
Meaning that you cannot use this

data.title: Show HN: AG-UI Protocol – Bring Agents into Frontend Applications
data.author: swiftlyTyped
data.article_summary: AG-UI 是一个开源、轻量级、基于事件的协议，旨在标准化 AI 代理与前端应用程序的交互。它定义了16种标准事件类型，支持多种事件传输方式（如SSE、WebSockets等），并提供了灵活的中间件层以确保跨环境兼容性。AG-UI 允许双向状态同步、实时上下文增强、生成式 UI 及更多功能，兼容多种流行代理框架如 LangGraph、Mastra、CrewAI 等。该协议提供了参考实现和客户端库，帮助开发者快速构建支持代理功能的应用。AG-UI 通过与社区和多个框架合作，确保其实用性和广泛适用性。更多信息和示例可在 ag-ui.com 查看。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AG-UI协议的发布及其在AI代理与前端应用交互中的作用

不同观点：
• [swiftlyTyped] 介绍了AG-UI协议，强调其作为一个开放、轻量级、基于事件的协议，旨在标准化AI代理如何与前端应用连接。该协议支持多种事件传输方式（如SSE, WebSockets, webhooks）并定义了16种标准事件类型，用于常见的代理-用户交互场景。AG-UI的发布伴随着与LangChain, Mastra, CrewAI等项目的集成，并且未来还会有更多合作。

• [dhorthy] 表示曾考虑过类似概念，称之为"MWP - model workload protocol"。该概念旨在通过客户端无关的方式（如SMS, WhatsApp, 内嵌应用, React组件）展示代理的工作状态，包括工作、思考、调用工具、出错、需要人工输入或批准等状态。

• [aatd86] 对AG-UI的具体用途存在疑问，不确定该协议是否用于提高可访问性或是一种新的UI构建范式。

• [Arindam1729] 对AG-UI表示兴奋，并计划尝试使用该协议，尤其是在MCP之后寻找新的解决方案。

• [nathan_tarbert] 对AG-UI表示高度赞赏，认为该协议将解决许多代理开发者面临的问题，并对其未来充满期待。

补充讨论：
• AG-UI协议的定位：在代理协议生态中，AG-UI专注于代理与人类用户在应用中的交互，而MCP负责代理与工具之间的通信，A2A/ACP则负责代理与代理之间的通信。

• 社区反应：AG-UI在发布后受到了积极的反馈，并且已经计划了工作组会议以进一步扩展和指导该协议的发展方向。

• 协议的实际应用场景：包括但不限于代理状态展示、错误处理、人工输入和批准等，涵盖了多种代理与用户交互的需求。

• 未来发展：AG-UI不仅有初步的集成伙伴，还计划与其他项目展开更多合作，显示出其在代理-用户交互领域的广泛应用潜力。

AG-UI: The Agent-User Interaction Protocol
AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes
how AI agents connect to front-end applications
.
➡️ See demos of AG-UI-enabled applications
here
AG-UI Specification
AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol for agent-human interaction, designed simplicity & flexibility:
During agent executions, agent backends
emit events
compatible
with one of AG-UI's 16 standard event types
Agent backends can
accept one of a few simple AG-UI compatible inputs
as arguments
AG-UI includes a flexible middleware layer
that ensures compatibility across diverse environments:
Works with
any event transport
(SSE, WebSockets, webhooks, etc.)
Allows for
loose event format matching
, enabling broad agent and app interoperability
It also ships with a
reference HTTP implementation
and
default connector
to help teams get started fast.
Learn more at ag-ui.com
Why AG-UI?
AG-UI was developed based on real-world requirements and practical experience building in-app agent interactions.
It was shaped through:
Working with users in the CopilotKit community to understand the needs of agent-based interactions in applications
Collaborating closely with leading agent frameworks (LangGraph, Mastra, CrewAI, AG2, etc.)

data.title: Pgwatch: PostgreSQL Monitoring Solution
data.author: klaussilveira
data.article_summary:
PGWATCH 是一个用于监控 PostgreSQL 数据库的解决方案，提供指标展示和仪表板功能。它使用 Docker 部署，包含 Grafana 作为展示工具，并通过 WebUI 或命令行添加和管理数据库。主要步骤包括：

1. 使用 Docker 运行 PGWATCH 镜像，暴露 Grafana（端口3000）、Web UI（端口8080）和数据库（端口5432）。
2. 通过内置 WebUI 或脚本添加测试数据库。
3. 使用 pgbench 脚本模拟数据库负载。
4. 使用 pgAdmin4 检查数据库内容，默认端口为80，可修改配置使用其他端口。
5. 开发过程中，修改代码后可以通过 Docker Compose 命令重新构建和启动服务。

PGWATCH 适用于开发和生产环境，提供快速部署和自定义监控仪表板的功能。

data.title: C is not a low-level language (2018)
data.author: pdubroy
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了C语言是否仍是一种低级语言，尤其是在Meltdown和Spectre漏洞暴露了现代处理器的复杂性之后。文章指出，C语言曾是低级语言，尤其在PDP-11计算机上，因为它直接映射了硬件操作。然而，现代处理器为了兼容C语言的抽象模型，加入了大量复杂性，如指令级并行（ILP），导致漏洞产生。现代处理器通过推测执行和缓存层次来提升性能，但这些对C程序员不可见，使得优化代码变得困难。文章认为，C语言已不再是真正的低级语言，因为它隐藏了现代处理器的许多复杂机制，而GPU等其他架构通过显式并行性实现了高性能，无需依赖ILP。因此，C语言提供的抽象模型已不再符合底层硬件的实际情况。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C语言是否为低级语言

不同观点：
• [empw] 认为根据一些论据，汇编语言也不一定是低级语言，暗示对C是否为低级语言的定义存在争议。
• [efitz] 坚持认为C是低级语言，并反驳了empw的观点，指出其论证中的矛盾，即在承认C符合低级语言定义的同时又否认C是低级语言。
• [Const-me] 认为虽然通过构建足够智能的编译器可以让C代码快速运行，但学习SIMD intrinsics（单指令多数据流内在函数）比解决编译器自动向量化问题更为可行，并提供了关于C和C++中SIMD扩展的文章链接，强调C++在特定硬件操作中的实用性。
• [variadix] 认为只要一种语言具有内联汇编功能或能够与汇编对象链接和交互，就应视为低级语言，因为这是硬件面向编程的必要条件。
• [OSDeveloper] 认为只有用于系统编程或内核开发的语言才算低级语言，例如Linux或OpenBSD的内核开发。
• [andrewmcwatters] 引用一句话讽刺性地指出，所有编程语言在某种程度上都可以被视为低级语言。
• [mystified5016] 反驳了认为C不是低级语言的观点，指出在微控制器和简单CPU（如68000、RISC、AVR）上，C仍然被广泛使用，并且在这些平台上，C与汇编非常接近，开发者仍需手动操作CPU寄存器和管理内存。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于C语言是否为低级语言，特别是在现代x86处理器和简单CPU（如68000、RISC、AVR）上的使用情况。
• mystified5016指出，即使现代x86处理器复杂度增加，C在简单CPU上仍然是低级语言，因为其直接操作硬件的特性。
• Const-me的文章链接提供了一个实际的例子，展示了C和C++中如何使用SIMD intrinsics进行硬件特定操作。
• 讨论中还涉及了低级语言的定义和标准，不同参与者对低级语言的理解和要求各不相同。

Current Issue
Past Issues
Topics
April 30, 2018
Volume 16, issue 2
PDF
C Is Not a Low-level Language
Your computer is not a fast PDP-11.
David Chisnall
In the wake of the recent Meltdown and Spectre vulnerabilities, it's worth spending some time looking at root causes. Both of these vulnerabilities involved processors speculatively executing instructions past some kind of access check and allowing the attacker to observe the results via a side channel. The features that led to these vulnerabilities, along with several others, were added to let C programmers continue to believe they were programming in a low-level language, when this hasn't been the case for decades.
Processor vendors are not alone in this. Those of us working on C/C++ compilers have also participated.
What Is a Low-Level Language?
Computer science pioneer Alan Perlis defined low-level languages this way:
"A programming language is low level when its programs require attention to the irrelevant."
5
While, yes, this definition applies to C, it does not capture what people desire in a low-level language. Various attributes cause people to regard a language as low-level. Think of programming languages as belonging on a continuum, with assembly at one end and the interface to the Starship
Enterprise
's computer at the other. Low-level languages are "close to the metal," whereas high-level languages are closer to how humans think.
For a language to be "close to the metal," it must provide an abstract machine that maps easily to the abstractions exposed by the target platform. It's easy to argue that C was a low-level language for the PDP-11. They both described a model in which programs executed sequentially, in which memory was a flat space, and even the pre- and post-increment operators cleanly lined up with the PDP-11 addressing modes.
Fast PDP-11 Emulators
The root cause of the Spectre and Meltdown vulnerabilities was that processor architects were trying to build not just fast processors, but fast processors that expose the same abstract machine as a PDP-11. This is essential because it allows C programmers to continue in the belief that their language is close to the underlying hardware.
C code provides a mostly serial abstract machine (until C11, an entirely serial machine if nonstandard vendor extensions were excluded). Creating a new thread is a library operation known to be expensive, so processors wishing to keep their execution units busy running C code rely on ILP (instruction-level parallelism). They inspect adjacent operations and issue independent ones in parallel. This adds a significant amount of complexity (and power consumption) to allow programmers to write mostly sequential code. In contrast, GPUs achieve very high performance without any of this logic, at the expense of requiring explicitly parallel programs.
The quest for high ILP was the direct cause of Spectre and Meltdown. A modern Intel processor has up to 180 instructions in flight at a time (in stark contrast to a sequential C abstract machine, which expects each operation to complete before the next one begins). A typical heuristic for C code is that there is a branch, on average, every seven instructions. If you wish to keep such a pipeline full from a single thread, then you must guess the targets of the next 25 branches. This, again, adds complexity; it also means that an incorrect guess results in work being done and then discarded, which is not ideal for power consumption. This discarded work has visible side effects, which the Spectre and Meltdown attacks could exploit.
On a modern high-end core, the register rename engine is one of the largest consumers of die area and power. To make matters worse, it cannot be turned off or power gated while any instructions are running, which makes it inconvenient in a dark silicon era when transistors are cheap but powered transistors are an expensive resource. This unit is conspicuously absent on GPUs, where parallelism again comes from multiple threads rather than trying to extract instruction-level parallelism from intrinsically scalar code. If instructions do not have dependencies that need to be reordered, then register renaming is not necessary.
Consider another core part of the C abstract machine's memory model: flat memory. This hasn't been true for more than two decades. A modern processor often has three levels of cache in between registers and main memory, which attempt to hide latency.
The cache is, as its name implies, hidden from the programmer and so is not visible to C. Efficient use of the cache is one of the most important ways of making code run quickly on a modern processor, yet this is completely hidden by the abstract machine, and programmers must rely on knowing implementation details of the cache (for example, two values that are 64-byte-aligned may end up in the same cache line) to write efficient code.
Optimizing C
One of the common attributes ascribed to low-level languages is that they're fast.

• Const-me的文章链接提供了一个实际的例子，展示了C和C++中如何使用SIMD intrinsics进行硬件特定操作。
• 讨论中还涉及了低级语言的定义和标准，不同参与者对低级语言的理解和要求各不相同。

data.title: GM says new battery chemistry will enable 400-mile range EVs
data.article_summary: 通用汽车（GM）与LG合作开发锂锰富集（LMR）电池，目标是将其用于未来的电动卡车和SUV。这种新电池化学技术更安全、能量密度更高且成本更低，因使用更便宜且丰富的锰，减少了对昂贵且涉及人权问题的钴的依赖。LMR电池的棱柱形设计提高了空间效率，使电动车的续航里程达到400英里。GM计划在2028年前在美国开始商业生产，并通过其与LG的合资企业Ultium Cells进行生产。尽管LMR材料面临容量损失和热稳定性问题，GM表示有信心通过创新解决这些挑战。这一进展旨在降低电动车成本，推动行业向电动化转型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电动汽车的电池技术和续航能力的未来发展及其实用性

不同观点：
• [blendo] 提到Stellantis和Factorial计划在2028年在美国开始商业化生产固态电池，并声称这种电池将在2026年用于Dodge Charger车型。这表明一些厂商正在推动电池技术的革新以提高续航能力。

• [mikestew] 认为虽然Lucid汽车已经可以达到400英里的续航，但文章中提到的300英里的Cadillac在使用新技术后可以增加33%的续航。他质疑“33%的续航增加”是否如宣传的那样吸引人。

• [nothercastle] 指出400英里的标称EPA续航在实际使用中可能接近300英里，并认为这样的续航已经相当不错。这反映了标称续航与实际使用续航之间的差距。

• [dev1ycan] 提到CATL的电池技术已经可以达到近500英里的续航，暗示电池技术的快速发展使得高续航变得越来越可行。

• [incomingpain] 强调充电速度和充电曲线比最大续航更为重要，指出像Chevy Bolt这样的车型由于缺乏热泵，在使用暖气时会显著消耗能量和续航。他还提到高档车型的充电速度可以达到150-300kw，而Bolt只有55kw，因此在长途驾驶中，充电速度显得尤为关键。

• [readthenotes1] 认为当前厂商在追求续航能力的提升是错误的策略，应该更多地关注减少充电时间，例如通过简化电池更换等方式来实现。

补充讨论：
• 续航能力的实际应用与标称值之间的差异是讨论的重点之一，尤其是实际驾驶中续航的缩水问题。
• 充电速度和充电曲线的优化被认为是提升电动汽车使用体验的关键因素，尤其是对于长途驾驶而言。
• 电池技术的不同发展方向，如固态电池和快速充电技术，以及它们对未来电动汽车市场的影响。
• 关于电池更换等其他创新方式的讨论，展示了对于如何提升电动汽车使用效率的不同思路。

争议焦点：
• 厂商是否应该优先提升续航能力，还是应该更多地关注充电时间和基础设施的改进。
• 标称续航与实际续航之间的差距及其对消费者选择的影响。

43974662.article_content:
News
GM says new battery chemistry will enable 400-mile range EVs
The automaker is pairing up with LG to develop lithium manganese-rich prismatic cells for its future electric trucks and SUVs. ﻿
The automaker is pairing up with LG to develop lithium manganese-rich prismatic cells for its future electric trucks and SUVs. ﻿
by
Andrew J. Hawkins
May 13, 2025, 2:00 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Andrew J. Hawkins
is transportation editor with 10+ years of experience who covers EVs, public transportation, and aviation. His work has appeared in The New York Daily News and City & State.
General Motors is teaming up with LG to develop lithium manganese-rich (LMR) batteries for its electric trucks and SUVs. The automaker says that the new chemistry is safer, more energy dense, and less costly than the current technology.
GM aims to become the first automaker to deploy LMR batteries in EVs, with plans to start commercial production in the US by 2028. Last month, Ford announced that it would start adopting LMR batteries for its EVs, but not until 2030.
In EV batteries, the cathode, or negative electrode, are typically made with NCM — nickel, cobalt, and magnesium. Cobalt is
a key component in this mix
, but it’s also the most expensive material in the battery and
mined under conditions that often violate human rights
, leading it to be called the “blood diamond of batteries.” As a result, GM and other companies
like Tesla
are rushing to create a cobalt-free battery. As an alternative, LMR battery cells use a higher proportion of more affordable and plentiful manganese, while also delivering greater capacity and energy density.
GM has prototyped approximately 300 full-size LMR cells as it worked with LG Energy Solution to crack the code on the chemistry.
An employee holds a full-size prototype LMR battery cell at the General Motors Wallace Battery Cell Innovation Center.
Image: GM
“We like to joke that it’s as cheap as dirt,” says Andrew Oury, a battery engineer at GM, referring to manganese.
GM’s current crop of electric Chevys and Cadillacs use high-nickel batteries, which supply enough energy for around 300–320 miles of range. The new LMR batteries are denser, with greater space efficiency due to their prismatic shape, enabling up to 400 miles of range, GM says. Prismatic cells are packed flat in rigid cases and are generally thought to be less complex to manufacture than cylindrical cells.
Less complexity and cheaper materials will hopefully lead to lower-cost EVs, which has been a significant challenge for the auto industry’s shift to electric vehicles.
“The EV growth rate is really dependent on how quickly we can bring the costs down over time,” says GM’s VP for batteries Kurt Kelty. “And this is the biggest lever we have. Batteries make up roughly 30 to 40 percent of the cost of vehicles. And if you can drop that down significantly like we’re doing here, then it ends up being a lower cost to the consumer.”
The cells will be produced by Ultium Cells, GM and LG’s joint venture, with preproduction expected to begin in late 2027. The final design will be validated at GM’s Battery Cell Development Center in Warren, Michigan, which opens earlier that year, as well as LG Energy Solution’s facility. Last year, GM sold its stake in the Lansing-based EV battery factory to LG.
“We like to joke that it’s as cheap as dirt.”
GM says the LMR batteries are the result of “decades-long research and investment in technology” that will give it the leg up over its competitors. GM began researching manganese-rich lithium-ion battery cells in 2015, including prototyping LMR cells at its Wallace Battery Cell Innovation Center.
There could be some challenges to mass producing LMR batteries. LMR materials have been known to experience significant capacity loss, which could lead to lower driving ranges and thermal stability degradation.
GM says it is aware of these challenges and confident that it could innovate the production process in a way to minimize those risks. The automaker’s engineers say the LMR batteries were expected to perform similarly to GM’s first-generation high-nickel batteries, even in extreme temperatures.
Automakers are racing to slash EV costs before
President Donald Trump’s trade war
raises the prices for key materials imported from China, which is the world’s leading producer of EV batteries, with over 70 percent of global lithium-ion battery production taking place there.
“We expect our localization of materials for the battery supply chain to increase between now and 2028,” Kelty says. “And LMR is part of that story, because we get more of the materials locally.”

data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 研究人员开发了一种锌离子微电容器，结合了电池和超级电容器的优点，适用于小型设备。这种微电容器具有高能量密度和快速充放电能力，能够在更小的尺寸下提供稳定的能量存储和快速供电。相比传统电池，锌离子微电容器更安全、环保，且制造成本较低。该技术有望在可穿戴设备、微型传感器等领域找到应用空间，填补电池和超级电容器之间的市场空白。

data.author: farslan
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者三年前偶然发现伦敦巴比肯建筑群，并对其产生浓厚兴趣，最终在近期访问伦敦时亲自参观的经历。巴比肯建于1965至1976年，是一个自给自足的综合住宅区，拥有住宅、停车场、学校和商业设施。其设计复杂如迷宫，细节处处体现古老埃及和军事元素，甚至包含古罗马和中世纪遗迹以及一个千年历史的犹太墓地。住宅区内部分区域仅对居民开放，居民通过电子钥匙进入隐藏通道。巴比肯还设有音乐学校分校，并因其独特设计成为媒体、建筑师和设计师的热门地点。作者推荐了几本关于巴比肯的书籍，供有兴趣者深入了解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：伦敦巴比肯中心的各种特点和体验

不同观点：
• **欣赏巴比肯的独特性**：[petercooper] 认为巴比肯是一个舒适、安静、艺术氛围浓厚的地方，能让人感受到文化和智慧的提升，且交通便利，停车方便。他还提到巴比肯没有商业连锁店，但有一家出色的音乐商店。
• **停车问题和居住困扰**：[yardie] 分享了自己在巴比肯购买公寓后遇到的地下停车场问题，包括废弃车辆难以处理的情况，反映了居住在此可能遇到的实际问题。
• **迷宫般的结构和导航困难**：[oniony] 提到巴比肯中心的迷宫结构和容易迷路的特点，特别是缺乏明确的指引，导致许多死胡同和需要钥匙或门卡才能通过的金属门。
• **文化设施和历史**：[rjmunro] 强调巴比肯的音乐厅和剧院是伦敦著名的文化场所，特别是伦敦交响乐团和皇家莎士比亚公司的常驻地，并提供相关历史链接。
• **生活体验和公共设施问题**：[chrisstu] 对巴比肯的公共厕所问题和老旧设施提出了批评，但也指出这些问题某种程度上增加了巴比肯的“魅力”。
• **高昂的维护费用和租赁年限**：[frereubu] 提到巴比肯公寓的高额服务费和租赁年限问题，指出虽然公寓本身不错，但费用和年限限制可能影响购买决策。

补充讨论：
• **建筑设计和城市生活理念**：[rriley] 将巴比肯与全球其他类似的乌托邦式建筑项目进行比较，如Walden 7、Arcosanti、Unité d'Habitation和Auroville，强调巴比肯不仅是一个居住空间，也是一种关于城市生活的理念表达。
• **建筑的三维特性**：[Ericson2314] 提到 brutalism 建筑风格的三维特性，以及巴比肯的 elevated walkways 带来的层次感和视觉体验。
• **影视取景地和公众关注**：[xnx] 指出巴比肯因在《Andor 2》中的场景拍摄而受到更多关注，链接了相关讨论。
• **个人偏好和审美争议**：[mjamil] 对巴比肯的美学持批评态度，认为它是 brutalist 浪潮的丑陋遗留，并表示自己会避免经过此地。相反，[nephrenka] 则在参加软件会议时对巴比肯的 brutalist 美学表示欣赏。

争议的焦点：
• **巴比肯的美学价值**：有人欣赏其文化和建筑独特性，认为它是智慧和文化的象征；也有人批评其 brutalist 风格丑陋，是过时的建筑遗留。
• **实际居住问题**：包括废弃车辆处理困难、公共设施老旧等实际问题与高昂的维护费用之间的矛盾。

43964136.article_content:
Three years ago, while searching for Vitsoe setups, I stumbled upon
Barbican
. I delved deeper and discovered a building complex that was beyond my imaginations.
Young Fatih would definitely find it ugly; current me finds it beautiful. The estate was built between 1965 and 1976. And, since I first saw it, I started watching and reading everything I could find. There are a few YouTube videos where you can peek into the lives of the residents. And there are a few books as well.
Of course, my dream was to visit the actual place. Stay there for a few hours, and discover more about this grandiose place. When I had a chance to visit London a few weeks ago, I planned to visit the estate. I had to.
While researching, I discovered that Barbican was far more than I had imagined. The residents offered
architecture tours
, and I couldn’t resist the opportunity to attend one. I invited two friends along, and we embarked on a 2-hour-long tour.
The tour, which took almost two hours, felt like it was just 10 minutes long. Our tour guide informed us with hundreds of small details, a few of which stuck in my mind in no particular order. Here are some of them (
all the photos where shoot with the Leica M11 + 35mm Summilux FLE btw)
Someone could start living as a single, marry someone, have kids, the kids could move out, the residents could die all in the same place. It has all the amenities someone would need to live there.
It's by design, created like a maze so people get lost. The tour guide even made a joke that there were no thieves in the Barbican, because once in, they don't know how to get out. (nit:
our Tour Guide said a few times how he felt like he lives in a Prison where volunteers would pay to live there
)
There’s an underground parking garage for the residents, but half of it is empty and filled with 20-30-year-old cars whose owners are no longer known.
Buildings are named after famous English people lived in their times (i.e: Shakespeare tower)
The architects were inspired by ancient Egyptians and Battalions. A specific Egyptian Cartouche, resembling a rounded rectangle, is almost universally found.
The rounded cartouche can be seen almost in every detail if you look carefully.
There are places that only residents can enter, some of which are completely hidden from the public. The residents have a key fob that can open doors and hidden gateways, allowing them to enter the Barbican even directly from the underground subway.
The Slow Horses laundry scenes were shot in Barbican.
The Laundry in the Slow Horses TV Show takes place in the Barbican
It was literally built on Roman and the Medieval ruins.
A corner of the Roman city
Londinium
can be found here. The Roman ruins were heavily modified though in the middle age. So the ruins have layers spanning hundreds of years.
It contains a
A 1000 year old Jewish burial ground as well
.
Jewish burial ground remains can be seen in the bottom left part.
There is central heating only, residents can't turn them off in the winter, leading to weird states where it gets just too hot or too cold sometimes.
The residents even have their own online forum sharing news/issues and recommendations between each other:
barbicantalk.com
Each building has details that are an ode to certain famous architects and designers, such as Le Corbusier.
Look carefully and you see various hints
It's popular among media, architects and designers. Hence there is always a public photo or video shooting.
There is a
branch of a Music school
inside Barbican, and some parts of the building resembling a
tuning fork
.
Barbican is full of treasures.
After reading this you might be interested to learn more. Here are a few Book recommendations:
Barbican Residents
: The book is mostly an interior design book, but only from people living in the various apartments in the Barbican Estate. Definitely a must buy if you're interested how the residents live there.
Barbican Estate
: Released in 2019, it's a heavy coffee table book with lots of gorgeous photos about the Barbican
Building Utopia: The Barbican Centre
: This book was released in 2022, and is currently the most up-to-date book about the Barbican.  It is compiled by Nicholas Kenyon, the Barbican Centre's Managing Director 2007–2021, hence contains a lot of unknown information.

data.title: Qwen3 Technical Report [pdf]
data.author: nkko
data.article_summary: QwenLM（如Qwen3）是一个开源的大语言模型项目，拥有广泛关注和较高的星标数量（如20.9k）。该项目托管在公共代码平台上，用户需登录以更改通知设置。用户可以 fork 或标星该项目，表明其在开发者社区中具有较高的影响力和活跃度。QwenLM 可能涉及先进的语言理解和生成能力，适用于多种文本相关的应用和研究。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）的发展方向应侧重于语言覆盖范围的扩展还是人类反馈的运用

不同观点：
• Grimblewald认为应减少对人类反馈的依赖，更多地关注语言覆盖范围的扩展。他指出，依赖人类反馈的模型往往变得谄媚和缺乏独立性，模型会盲目迎合用户的观点，而不是提供真实、必要的反馈。他更倾向于模型产生“幻觉”（hallucinations），即生成并非严格基于输入的内容，因为这比模型仅仅为了讨好用户而提供反馈要好。

• Grimblewald进一步支持扩展语言覆盖范围的论据是基于语言学研究，指出不同文化在描述世界时有不同的优先级和分辨率，某些文化对特定方面的词汇更为丰富。因此，扩大语言覆盖范围有助于模型更好地理解无法通过直接体验获得的世界知识，并加深其对世界的理解。

补充讨论：
• Grimblewald认为语言本身承载着文化的价值观和优先级，因此通过扩展语言覆盖范围，模型能够获得对世界更深刻的洞察力。他认为这是比依赖人类反馈更有效的提升模型理解力的方式。

• 争议的焦点在于人类反馈和语言覆盖范围之间的平衡。Grimblewald显然更倾向于扩展语言覆盖范围，认为这样能使模型获得更广泛、更深刻的理解，但他也承认人类反馈有其存在的价值，只是过度依赖会导致模型失去独立性和客观性。

总结来看，评论中讨论的核心在于LLM的发展路径，一方观点强调减少人类反馈依赖以避免模型变得谄媚和缺乏独立性，另一方观点则认为扩展语言覆盖范围有助于模型更全面地理解世界。

data.title: Microsoft laying off 6k employees
data.author: friendofkoalas
data.article_summary: 微软宣布将裁员6,000多人，约占公司员工总数的3%。这是继2023年裁员10,000人后的最大规模裁员，影响范围包括微软旗下业务如LinkedIn和部分国际办公室。此次裁员旨在提高公司市场敏捷性，减少管理层级。近一年来，微软已多次裁员，包括2024年关闭多家游戏工作室和裁减Xbox及HoloLens团队员工。此次裁员也紧随公司CFO Amy Hood提出的精简管理层的计划。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI公司的投资回报和股东行为

不同观点：
• [gmerc] 认为AI公司目前没有产生投资回报（ROI），并且如果这些公司在未来1-2个季度未达到增长预期，股东将会无情地抛售股票。这暗示了AI行业目前面临较大的财务压力，股东对增长的短期预期非常高。

• [ChrisArchitect] 没有直接表达观点，而是提供了一个链接，暗示该话题可能在其他讨论中已有涉及（链接指向了一个Hacker News的讨论帖，id为43973399）。这可能意味着他/她认为这个话题并非新鲜话题，或者已有现成的讨论和分析。

补充讨论：
• [gmerc] 的评论指向了对AI公司财务表现和股东预期的关注，尤其是股东对季度增长的敏感性。这反映了AI行业在资本市场中面临的短期业绩压力。

• [ChrisArchitect] 的回应则引导读者参考其他讨论，可能认为已有的讨论已经足够涵盖当前话题，或者认为当前话题缺乏新的讨论价值。

争议焦点：AI公司的短期财务表现与股东预期间的矛盾，以及是否需要进一步讨论。

Microsoft is laying off more than 6,000 employees
Microsoft employees have faced a series of layoffs over the past year.
Microsoft employees have faced a series of layoffs over the past year.
by
Tom Warren
May 13, 2025, 3:23 PM UTC
Link
Facebook

Image: Cath Virginia / The Verge
Tom Warren
is a senior editor and author of
Notepad
, who has been covering all things Microsoft, PC, and tech for over 20 years.
Microsoft announced on Tuesday that it’s laying off more than 6,000 employees, around three percent of the company’s entire workforce. These are the biggest job cuts at Microsoft since it
laid off 10,000 employees
in 2023, and will impact employees across Microsoft’s businesses.
“We continue to implement organizational changes necessary to best position the company for success in a dynamic marketplace,” says Microsoft spokesperson Pete Wootton in a statement to
The Verge
.
I understand that the job cuts will impact all levels at Microsoft, including Microsoft-owned LinkedIn and some international offices. The cuts come just weeks after Microsoft CFO Amy Hood hinted at reducing the company’s management layers. “We continue to focus on building high-performing teams and increasing our agility by reducing layers with fewer managers,”
said Hood on April 30th
. Microsoft also started ”
performance-based” cuts
earlier this year, which have targeted hundreds of employees.
The latest job losses come more than a year after Microsoft
laid off 1,900 Activision Blizzard and Xbox employees
, and then in May 2024 the company
closed several game studios
, including
Hi-Fi Rush
developer Tango Gameworks and
Redfall
developer Arkane Austin. Tango Gameworks later returned thanks to a
deal with Krafton
.
Microsoft also
laid off 650 more Xbox employees
in September, as part of a restructuring related to the company’s acquisition of Activision Blizzard. Microsoft also
cut around 1,000 employees
from its HoloLens and Azure cloud teams in June.

data.title: Nissan to slash 11,000 jobs, close 7 plants
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 日产（Nissan）宣布大规模裁员和工厂关闭计划，将再削减11,000个工作岗位，并关闭7家工厂，这将使公司的生产工厂从17家减少到10家。此次裁员后，日产的员工总数将减少约20,000人，占其全球员工总数的15%。目前，日产在全球拥有超过133,000名员工。新任CEO伊万·埃斯皮诺萨（Ivan Espinosa）表示，公司的可变成本上升，固定成本高于当前收入支持的水平，财务结果是一个“警钟”。这些举措是在日产面临销售下滑和管理层变动等挑战的背景下做出的。此前，日产曾宣布取消在日本建设新工厂的计划，并退出了与本田的合并谈判。分析人士认为，日产暂时不会倒闭。

Nissan layoffs: Company to slash another 11,000 jobs, close 7 plants
Natalie Neysa Alund
USA TODAY
Hear this story
Nissan on May 13 announced sweeping cuts across the company with plans to lay off another 11,000 employees and close more than a half-dozen plants across the globe.
The latest cuts bring the carmaker's total workforce reduction to roughly 20,000 jobs, which accounts for 15% of the Japan-based automakers workforce, according to
Reuters
and
The Associated Press.
Following a whirlwind year, the company announced it would also close seven plants, Reuters reported. The move will cut the number of its production plants from 17 to 10.
It was not immediately clear which positions were being slashed and which plants were shuttering.
USA TODAY has reached out to Nissan.
Need a break?
Play the USA TODAY Daily Crossword Puzzle.
Financial results a 'wake-up call,' CEO says
Nissan employs more than 133,000 people worldwide, according to
Nissan's Global website
, with about 21,000 people, including manufacturing employees, in the United States.
The new layoffs will bring Nissan's total workforce cuts to about 20,000 jobs. Last year, the automaker announced plans to cut 9,000 workers and previously announced nixing plans to build a plant in Japan.
"As you can see, our full-year financial results are a wake-up call," newly named CEO Ivan Espinosa said during a press conference, according to Reuters and
The Japan Times
. The reality is very clear. Our variable costs are rising. Our fixed costs are higher than our current revenue can support."
Espinosa, who replaced former CEO Makoto Uchida (2019-2025) recently revealed a handful of upcoming vehicles to the public recently including
the new Leaf EV and the Kicks
.
The hidden costs of owning a car:
How fuel, maintenance and depreciation add up
Nissan layoffs come after retreating on merger
The move comes on the heels of Nissan facing a plethora of challenges including new management, falling sales, and potential merger or acquisition. But analysts don’t see the company failing anytime soon, the
Detroit Free Press
, part of the USA TODAY Network reported last month.
In December 2024, Nissan and Honda
announced a plan to merge
, but Nissan retreated from the negotiations in February.
This is a developing story.
Contributing: Reuters; Mark Phelan with The Detroit Free Press
Natalie Neysa Alund is a senior reporter for USA TODAY. Reach her at nalund@usatoday.com and follow her on X @nataliealund.

data.title: A simple 16x16 dot animation from simple math rules
data.author: andrewrn
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Tixy，一个创意代码高尔夫游戏。玩家需用不超过32个字符的代码实现特定效果，代码格式为`(t, i, x, y) =>`。通过点击页面上的点可以获取更多信息。Tixy旨在以简洁的代码创作出复杂的图形或动画效果，考验编程技巧和创意。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Tixy平台及其类似项目的评价与创作分享

不同观点：
• **欣赏与喜爱**：
  - 多名用户表达了对Tixy的喜爱，并分享了自己基于Tixy创作的动画和图案，例如[animal531]、[Nautman]、[progre]、[franze]等，展示了各种创意作品，包括模拟白细胞攻击、风屏雨刷效果、火焰效果、以及圣诞主题动画。
  
• **教育用途**：
  - [jakegmaths]提到利用Tixy与计算机科学学生互动，创建了包含谜题的Tixy网格，学生们对此非常感兴趣，显示了Tixy在教育中的潜在应用价值。

• **类似项目分享**：
  - [stankot]分享了自己创建的类似项目Pulsar，并提到了另一个使用HTML滑块的项目Sliderland，展示了与Tixy类似的动画效果。
  - [rpastuszak]介绍了一个受Tixy启发的绘画应用，具有可编程笔刷功能，强调了时间动态而非压力或倾斜度。

• **技术背景与作者**：
  - [agys]指出了Tixy的作者Martin Kleppe及其在JavaScript魔术代码方面的成就，提供了相关链接，让讨论扩展到作者的其他项目。

• **对平台的简化评价**：
  - [levzettelin]将Tixy比喻为“为傻瓜设计的Shadertoy”，暗示Tixy是一个更易上手的版本，适合喜欢简化创作流程的用户。

补充讨论：
• **过往讨论与资源**：
  - [asicsp]提供了之前关于Tixy模式的讨论链接，指向Hacker News上的评论，为有兴趣的用户提供了更多背景资料。

争议焦点：
• 评论中未见明显争议，主要为用户分享各自的作品与类似项目，整体氛围积极且充满创意互动。

data.author: toomuchtodo
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：评论围绕数据图表的呈现方式及其反映的实际情况展开讨论，包括数据时间范围、图表设计以及全球与美国就业市场的比较。

不同观点：
• [ericmcer] 认为图表截止到2020年，没有展示更长的时间范围，如从2000年开始，这可能导致人们误解2020-2021年的剧烈变化是长期趋势，而非短期的波动。他建议延长图表时间线以展示更全面的趋势。

• [didgetmaster] 提出通过图表的起止时间判断故事的准确性，认为选择特定日期范围来展示最大变化是一种误导，例如从2023年10月11日开始，而不是以当前日期结束，这是一种警示信号。

• [senderista] 对图表的Y轴没有从零开始表示不满，认为这可能夸大变化幅度，影响对实际趋势的理解。

• [mainecoder] 反驳关于美国就业市场不利的说法，认为虽然美国的情况变得不那么有利，但许多发展中国家的情况更糟，因此更多人希望在美国工作。

• [toomuchtodo] 提供了一个报告链接，可能与讨论相关，但未具体阐述观点。

• [readthenotes1] 认为根据数据，全球净变化比美国更为显著，因此标题应强调“尽管全球就业市场降温，美国仍具吸引力”。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于图表的时间范围和设计是否故意操纵以展示更剧烈的变化，以及如何更准确地反映实际情况。
• 有人关注全球与美国就业市场的比较，讨论美国在全球就业市场中的相对吸引力。
• 图表设计细节（如Y轴起点）也被视为影响数据解读的重要因素。

data.title: CISA changes vulnerabilities updates, shifts to X and emails
data.author: Corrado
data.article_summary: 美国网络安全和基础设施安全局（CISA）宣布，今后仅在网站上发布与紧急威胁或重大网络活动相关的警报，常规更新和指导将通过电子邮件、RSS和埃隆·马斯克的社交平台X发布。此举旨在确保关键信息得到更多关注并易于查找。同时，其他政府机构如国家运输安全委员会和社会保障局也逐渐将更多通信转移至X平台。前CISA主管批评此举，称预算削减将削弱美国的网络防御能力。这一变化可能与CISA的人手削减和预算减少有关，而这些措施受到特朗普政府的影响。
